subject: Pricing: order schedule - 'saddle' anchoring and breach carveout (redlines)
messages:
From: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acmecloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: L. Ruiz <l.ruiz@acmelegal.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft redline for order schedule - pricing saddle + breach carveout

Marcus — attaching Acme’s suggested redline of the order schedule. We have a narrow window to finalize before our board sign-off next week (10/25). Key items we flagged: a) the “saddle” anchoring language in Exhibit B (we call it the price-saddle) — Acme wants clearer min/max guardrails tied to monthly invoice periods rather than annual true-ups; b) a breach-triggered uplift clause (Section 4.2) that would allow Redwood to raise price by up to 15% after certain usage breaches — our procurement team asks that this be constrained or removed; c) a request to add a mid-term reconciliation cap (we proposed a $X cap per quarter).

Can you confirm Redwood’s position and share a clean-marked copy back? I’ve attached our redline (acme_order_schedule_redline_v1.pdf).

Thanks,
Jamie
Jamie Patel
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Cloud
jamie.patel@acmecloud.com
(415) 555-0182

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline for order schedule - pricing saddle + breach carveout

Jamie — thanks for sending the redline and the clear bullets. Internal notes below and looping in Irene (sales+legal liaison) and Karthik (pricing/product) so we can converge quickly.

High-level response: we understand the concern on annual true-ups; we can discuss moving some of the guardrail math to monthly buckets, but we need to keep an annual true-up to reconcile usage spikes across product cycles (otherwise forecasting and capacity commitments break). The breach-triggered uplift (Section 4.2) is there to protect exposed shared capacity in extreme overload scenarios — but the 15% uplift in the draft is aggressive.

Next steps: Irene, can you take point with Acme Legal on the breach language and propose an alternative that caps uplift and ties it to objective metrics (e.g., sustained 95th-percentile utilization over two consecutive months)? Karthik — please confirm what quarterly cap we can tolerate for mid-term reconciliation and whether a hard $ cap per quarter (as Acme suggested) would be workable operationally.

We’ll produce a Redwood-marked PDF and an updated Excel schedule (redwood_pricing_schedule_v2.xlsx) by EOD tomorrow. If Acme can share examples of how they expect monthly guardrail math to operate (sample monthly invoices), that will speed things up.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Draft redline for order schedule - pricing saddle + breach carveout

Jamie — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear comments in the PDF. I’m attaching Redwood’s counter-redline (embedded below) and summarizing the proposed compromise so legal can assess quickly.

Summary of Redwood counter-proposals (high level):
- Price-saddle anchoring: we can rework Exhibit B to reference monthly invoice-band guardrails for short-term smoothing (useful for operational billing), but preserve an annual reconciliation clause that reconciles month-to-month variances. The wording we suggest: "Monthly invoice bands shall be used for interim billing; an annual reconciliation (within 45 days of the anniversary) will true up to the committed tier-based schedule."
- Breach-triggered uplift (Section 4.2): we cannot accept an unbounded removal of the uplift protection — however, we will replace the fixed 15% uplift with a tiered remediation uplift that: (a) requires objective trigger metrics (95th percentile sustained for 60 days), (b) caps uplift to 7% for the first occurrence and 12% for repeated occurrences within a rolling 12-month window, and (c) requires a remediation plan and written notice 30 days prior to any price change.
- Mid-term reconciliation cap: we can accept a per-quarter cap on recoveries, but propose it be expressed as a percentage of quarter spend rather than a fixed dollar cap ($) to scale with usage. Proposed: 18% of quarter spend.

Redline excerpt (quoted from our markup):

"Section 4.2 - Breach-Triggered Price Adjustment (Redwood proposed language):
In the event of sustained customer usage that materially exceeds the committed tier and causes measurable capacity strain (defined as sustained 95th-percentile utilization for sixty (60) consecutive days), Redwood may propose a remediation uplift not to exceed seven percent (7%) for the first occurrence. If the same customer exceeds the trigger twice within a rolling twelve (12) month period, Redwood may propose an uplift not to exceed twelve percent (12%). Redwood will provide Customer with thirty (30) calendar days' written notice describing the observed metrics, remediation steps, and proposed uplift. Any uplift shall be limited to the lesser of the uplift cap or the uplift required to cover demonstrable incremental serving costs incurred by Redwood.

The parties agree to meet promptly to review telemetry supporting any proposed uplift.
"

I’ll attach our marked PDF for legal review. If Acme can accept the objective trigger + capped uplift + notice requirement, we think this is a reasonable compromise that preserves predictable economics for both sides and avoids cliff pricing shocks.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood-inference.com

Attachment: redwood_counter_redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 55KB)

From: L. Ruiz <l.ruiz@acmelegal.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline for order schedule - pricing saddle + breach carveout

Irene / Marcus — thanks for the thoughtful counter. A few quick notes from Acme Legal after a rapid review: we can accept moving to monthly invoice bands + an annual true-up as you proposed, but we need the annual reconciliation window tightened to 30 days (rather than 45 days) given our internal finance timelines. On the breach uplift, Acme is reluctant to give any uplift over 5% absent a catastrophic outage event. That said, we could accept a tiered approach if Redwood will: (a) lower the first-occurrence cap to 5%, (b) lower the repeat-occurrence cap to 9%, and (c) include an explicit independent audit right (Auditor scope limited to telemetry used to justify the uplift). Finally, on the mid-term cap we prefer a hard-dollar cap because our procurement committees budget against $ amounts; alternatively, Acme will accept a % cap only if you supply an illustrative quarterly sample during negotiation.

Proposed path: accept monthly bands + 30-day annual true-up window; agree to the objective trigger but move uplift caps to 5%/9% and add the audit right. If Redwood accepts those edits, Acme Legal will sign off and we can move to DocuSign next week.

Please confirm and I’ll produce a small joint redline.

Regards,
L. Ruiz
Counsel, Acme Cloud Legal
l.ruiz@acmelegal.com
